rules.description: Brooks's bar counting, the H1/H2/H3/H4 and L1/L2/L3/L4 family. A persistent count of completed pullback legs since the trend last made a fresh resetLookback-bar high. A bar whose high exceeds the prior bar's high advances the count, but only once a new low has formed since the last counted bar (otherwise it is a retest of the same leg, not a new one); the count resets to 0 the instant the close makes a fresh resetLookback-bar high. Fires on the bar that advances the count to countTarget - that bar is the high-N signal bar, and under the corpus's stop-entry convention (signal-bar close, next-bar open) the fire IS the entry. Mirror: low 1..low 4.

complexity.reason: a cross-bar counter plus two remembered prices and one Highest window; no pivot detection and no lookahead

catalog_match.note: nothing in the catalog holds cross-bar counter state of this kind

rules.merge_notes: Twenty-three statements of one primitive, the single most load-bearing rule in the trilogy. THE DEFINITION THAT WINS IS R17-01 (Ranges ch17), for the reason MERGE.md gives: it needs no swing pivots, no lookahead and no leg definition - a bar advances the count on a higher high only after a new low since the last counted bar, and the count resets on a fresh N-bar high. Every other definition here is a citation, not a rule. The losing definitions, in the order they cost more machinery: (a) swing-pivot leg segmentation - R05-17, V24-03, TP1-05, T18-02, T20-02, V01-05, all graded hard and all needing SwingHigh/SwingLow plus pivot retention; (b) 'count each higher-high bar since the pullback began, resetting when the trend makes a new extreme' with the extreme left undefined - R00-61's R00-60, T00-20's T00-19, TP1-06 (this is R17-01 minus the concrete reset, which is exactly what R17-01 sharpens); (c) the ad hoc per-chapter counters T10-23 (reset on a new trend high, resetLookback 20 - the closest independent restatement of R17-01, and strong corroboration), T15-19 (resetOnNewHighBars 10), T21-72 (maxPullbackBars 20). The 'at least one bar that did not make a higher high between counts' phrasing (T10-23, T15-19, T21-72) is behaviourally the same guard as R17-01's 'a new low since the last counted bar' in a real pullback, but R17-01's is the cheaper and less ambiguous test and is the one carried. countTarget covers high 1 (R05-18, V00-52, R17-03, R01-09's 'first pullback', V01-10's pullback ordinal), high 2 (the most-stated setup: R05-19, V00-53, R17-04, T10-23, T15-19, T18-02, T20-02, T21-72, V01-05, TP1-06, T00-20, R00-61), high 3 (wedge bull flag) and high 4 (R17-06); Brooks caps the count at 4 and the counter saturates there. resetLookback defaults differ (R17-01/T10-23 20, T15-19 10, T21-72 20); 20 is carried. ABC corrections are this counter under another name - leg A is the run to count 1, leg B the failed bounce, leg C the run to count 2 - so no separate rule (R00-61, R17-01 and T01-05 all say so). ROLL-UP: swing_structure merged R17-01 alone under this same key with the same shape; the two entries are the same rule and only one should be authored. countTarget was added there for the same reason it is added here - a rule must fire on something. Folded the swing_structure copy (R17-01), the same persistent counter from the same source.

rules.description: The current pullback has completed AT LEAST minLegs legs - HighLowBarCount's counter read as a threshold rather than an equality. Brooks's 'a pullback, like all trends, will commonly have at least two legs': a with-trend entry is favoured only once the count has reached two.
rules.pseudocode: count >= minLegs   // the counter of HighLowBarCount, same state and same reset

complexity.reason: the HighLowBarCount counter with a >= comparison

rules.merge_notes: Kept apart from HighLowBarCount deliberately: == countTarget fires on ONE bar (the signal bar) while >= minLegs stays true for the rest of the pullback, so as a context filter ANDed into a pane they select different bars. All three sources state it as a context/quality read, not an entry: RP3-03 'a pullback commonly has at least two legs, fade the first leg's breakout and wait for the second'; V01-03 'it was two-legged, so the bears showed some strength' (its swing-pivot countLegs is the losing definition, replaced by the R17-01 counter); T19-21 'repeated two-legged pullbacks are setting up with-trend entries' - the REPETITION across successive pullbacks is dropped as having no bar-level test, so T19-21 is carried lossily as the single-pullback reading. Default 2 from all three.

rules.description: The pullback in progress has lasted no more than maxPullbackBars bars, measured as the bars since the trend last made a fresh resetLookback-bar high (the same anchor HighLowBarCount resets on). A brief pullback is Brooks's sign of strength; NEGATED, the rule is his sign of weakness ('the pullback extends for several bars').
rules.pseudocode: barsSince(close[0] > highest(high, resetLookback)[1]) <= maxPullbackBars

complexity.reason: a bars-since counter keyed on the same fresh-extreme test HighLowBarCount already computes

rules.merge_notes: One rule and the per-placement negate toggle. R02-15 / T00-34 / V00-49 are the strength form (<= 2 bars); R02-24 is the same test negated at a different threshold (>= 4 bars, weakness). Both book values recorded, default 2 (three sources against one). R02-15's and V00-49's second conjunct - 'and it follows a bar that is not a strong bear reversal bar' - is NOT carried here: bar_anatomy_reversal_signal already merged it as PullbackNotAfterStrongOppositeReversalBar, and the pane ANDs it. The anchor is the design decision that lets this leave research grade: the sources say 'the pullback' without saying when it started, and the fresh-N-bar-high reset from R17-01 supplies a concrete start with no pivot search. R11-11 (dropped) states the same measure as a WINDOW, 5 to 10 bars, for a high 2 - if the authoring pass wants a band, minPullbackBars is the second input to add.

rules.description: The first pullback bar after a breakout does not arrive until at least minBarsBeforePullback bars have passed since the breakout bar: the current bar is the first bar since the breakout whose low is below the prior bar's low, and it is at least N bars after it. Brooks's leading sign of breakout strength; NEGATED it is his sign of weakness ('the first pullback occurs two bars after the reversal').
rules.pseudocode:
b = barsSince(close[0] > highest(high, breakoutLookback)[1]);
b >= minBarsBeforePullback && low[0] < low[1] && lowest(low, b)[1] >= low[1]   // no earlier pullback bar since the breakout

complexity.reason: a bars-since-breakout counter plus a 'no earlier pullback bar' window test

rules.merge_notes: Eight statements of one test, five of them the same sentence copied across books ('The first pullback occurs only after three or more bars of breaking out' - R00-58, R02-14, V00-48, T00-33). Three add something. R05-02 is the same rule at minBarsBeforePullback = 0/1: it is the bare marker 'the first bar since the breakout with a low below the prior bar's low', which is where the 'no earlier pullback bar' clause in the pseudocode comes from and is the most mechanizable phrasing of the first-pullback anchor. R02-23 is the rule NEGATED (a pullback within 2 bars = weakness) - the per-placement toggle, both thresholds recorded. T15-40 is the OTHER bound, 'any pullback should come within five bars or so' - negated at minBarsBeforePullback = 6; its raceBars conjunct (consecutive higher highs since the breakout) is bar_anatomy_trend_doji's ConsecutiveTrendBars and is ANDed by the pane, not carried. V02-13 is the one source that mechanizes the anchor fully - 'the first down-close since a bull reversal bar k bars ago with k-1 up closes between' - and is the reason the grade is moderate rather than research; its anchor is a reversal bar rather than a breakout, which is a placement choice, not a different rule. Default 3, unanimous among the sources that state it. The breakout anchor uses the same fresh-N-bar-extreme test as HighLowBarCount so the two share one window.

rules.description: The high 1 in a strong bull spike: after spikeBars consecutive bull trend bars, the first bar whose low is below the prior bar's low is the signal bar, and the entry fires when a bar within maxWaitBars closes above that signal bar's high. Mirror: the low 1 after a bear spike.

complexity.reason: a 'spike seen, first pullback seen' state pair carried across an unknown number of bars, plus one retained price

catalog_match.note: the trigger term is CloseAbovePriorHigh against a RETAINED signal-bar high rather than a fixed lag, which the catalog rule cannot express

rules.merge_notes: Kept as a composite because it is a named Brooks setup ('buying a high 1 pullback in a strong bull spike', stated in all three) AND because the trigger is against a bar at a VARIABLE lag - the pane cannot AND CloseAbovePriorHigh(fixed lag) with a spike filter and get this. It is NOT HighLowBarCount at countTarget 1: this rule's reset is a completed spike, not a fresh N-bar high, and its trigger is a later bar closing over a retained level rather than the signal bar itself. spikeBars: T07-45 says 3, TP3-16 says 4, T23-04 says 3 - default 3. T23-04 is the same mechanism anchored at the session open ('trend from the open'), so its placement is INTRADAY-ONLY while the rule itself is not; the always-in / trend-from-open flag it also reads is a context_regime rule the pane ANDs. Brooks's caveat in TP3-16 and T07-45, 'but not after a buy climax', is PostClimaxCorrectionBlock and is ANDed, not carried here.

rules.description: The second entry: an earlier same-side signal triggered within the last withinBars bars, that first entry failed (price traded back beyond the first signal bar's opposite extreme), and a new same-side signal is triggering now. Brooks's most-repeated reliability filter, and the one condition he says is sufficient on its own.
rules.pseudocode: exists k in 2..withinBars: close[k] > high[k+1] && lowest(low, k-1)[0] < low[k+1] && close[0] > high[1]

complexity.reason: a bounded backward scan with two conditions per candidate bar; no pattern registry and no per-placement state

catalog_match.note: LastTradeCooldown gates on a REALIZED trade's outcome via PositionProfit/BarsSinceExit; this gates on a repeated raw pattern whether or not a trade was taken, and can fire before any trade exists

rules.merge_notes: Eight statements, and the fork that matters is what 'the same logic as the first signal' means. TWO OPTIONS were on the table. (1) A generic setup-identity registry - 'the same Entry candidate fired and failed' - which is what R00-52, V00-65, T00-21, T06-31 and R26-06 describe, all graded research, and which needs engine support the corpus does not have (a per-placement fire/fail log). (2) T21-28's CONCRETE PROXY: define the signal as the generic price trigger (a close above the prior bar's high) and the failure as price trading back below that signal bar's low, then scan the last withinBars bars for one. T21-28 WINS - it is a bounded scan over prices, needs no registry, and reproduces the second entry Brooks actually points at in the figures. It is lossy in exactly one way, and the loss should be recorded: it counts a second GENERIC trigger, not a second instance of whichever pattern is placed alongside it. Option 1 stays available if per-placement signal memory is ever added; bar_anatomy_reversal_signal reached the same conclusion for SecondReversalSignal and its 'track only the engine's own last Entry signal' decision is the third option. withinBars: T21-28 10, V24-18 8, V00-65 5, T06-31 10, R00-52 6, R26-06 10 - default 10. V04-13 is this filter with a climax anchor ('buy a higher low after a sell climax, not the initial reversal'), carried as a citation; the climax term is ANDed. Near-miss kept separate: SecondSignalNotBetterPrice is the price-quality gate ON this rule, not a restatement of it.

rules.description: The current signal bar's entry price is at or above the first signal bar's (mirror: at or below) - Brooks's trap test on a second entry: 'if the second entry is letting you in at a better price than the first, be suspicious. Most good second entries are at the same price or worse.'
rules.pseudocode: high[0] >= high[firstSignalBarIndex] - toleranceTicks * tickSize   // firstSignalBarIndex from the SecondSignal scan

complexity.reason: reuses SecondSignal's scan and compares one retained price

rules.merge_notes: Single source, kept as its own rule rather than folded into SecondSignal because it is a separate, independently meaningful test and Brooks states it as an override ('good fill, bad trade'); a placement can want the second entry without the price gate. It cannot be authored before SecondSignal, since it reads the same scan's first-signal bar. Figure 10.1's bar 10 is the book's counter-example: one tick better than bar 9, and it failed.

rules.description: A triggered high-N long (low-N short) fails: after HighLowBarCount reached countTarget, price trades back beyond the signal bar's opposite extreme. Brooks reads a failed high 4 / low 4 as the side losing control, and permits or takes the reversal trade in the other direction.
rules.pseudocode:
countReached = HighLowBarCount fired at countTarget on bar k;
close[0] < signalLow[k]   // long side failed -> permit/take the short

complexity.reason: the HighLowBarCount counter plus its already-retained signalLow and a bars-since cap

rules.merge_notes: Six statements of one event and its consequence. The event is identical in all six - a high-N or low-N setup triggered and then price went back through the signal bar - and the machinery is already inside HighLowBarCount (signalLow is retained there, so the failure test is free). countTarget default 4, the case Brooks names most (R00-62, V00-55, T00-48 all say low 4); T04-08 states it at 1 (fading a failed low 1 in a bottoming bear trend) and VP1-11 at 2/3 (a failed low 2 as a failed bear flag), so the same input covers all of them. Two sources add a conjunct that is NOT carried and is ANDed by the pane instead: T00-48 requires a bear trend-line break before the bears count as having regained control (a lines_channels_trendlines rule; TLValue recorded in el_words_needed for it), and VP1-11 requires the resulting breakout in the new direction (a breakouts rule). T00-48's framing is the negate toggle on this rule - block with-trend entries while the failure stands - so it needs no second rule. R00-62's 'wait for more price action' is advice with no test and is dropped from the reading.

rules.description: Exit a high-N long (low-N short) as soon as price trades back below the count's signal bar low (above its high) before the position has reached a scalper's profit. Brooks: 'if the market reverses and trades below the low of the pattern before reaching at least a scalper's profit, the high 2 buy has failed.'
rules.pseudocode: ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && low[0] < signalLow && ctx.OpenPositionProfit() < scalpProfitTicks * tickSize * bigPointValue

complexity.reason: reads HighLowBarCount's retained signalLow plus open-profit state

catalog_match.note: a stop at a PATTERN price (the signal bar's low) gated on not yet having made a scalper's profit, not a fixed dollar loss

rules.merge_notes: Single source, and an Exit, so it cannot be reached by placing FailedCountReversal in the exit pane (an Entry cannot sit there - the catalog makes the same call for ConsecutiveCloseExit). Same event as FailedCountReversal, opposite use: that one takes the other side, this one just gets out. R17-12's own note is worth keeping: a failed count usually becomes the next count number, which is simply HighLowBarCount continuing to advance, so no separate rule is needed for 'a failed high 2 becomes a high 3'.

rules.description: Exit (and optionally reverse) the open position the moment the OPPOSITE side's bar count reaches countTarget. Brooks: 'if you ever buy early, always get out and even reverse if the market triggers a low 2 or 3 short'; mirrored for a short caught by a high 2 or 3.
rules.pseudocode: ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && lowCount == countTarget

complexity.reason: the same counter as HighLowBarCount read on the opposite side, plus a position test

catalog_match.note: the catalog rule is an Entry-side reversal permission keyed on dollars; this is an Exit keyed on the opposing count triggering

rules.merge_notes: ROLL-UP: swing_structure merged V21-04 ('countertrend traders trying to buy in a bear trend should always exit on a low 2 signal') under this same key with the same shape - one rule, two sources across two buckets, author once. Kept as its own rule rather than a placement of HighLowBarCount because it reads the OPPOSITE side's counter, which a mirrored Entry placement cannot supply, and because it is an Exit. R17-13's 'especially if there is a strong bear signal bar' is a bar_anatomy_reversal_signal term with no threshold given and is dropped; the 'optionally reverse' half is the engine's own reversal behaviour, not a condition. Folded the swing_structure copy (V21-04): the same exit on the opposing count reaching countTarget.

rules.description: Suppress a fresh high 1 that follows a completed high-1(s)-then-high-2 sequence without an intervening deeper pullback: the counter has just advanced to 1 again, and the PREVIOUS count cycle had already reached at least minPriorCount. Brooks: 'after a series of winning trades, be suspicious of renewed strength without first seeing a larger pullback - it might be a trap setting up.'
rules.pseudocode:
// one extra persistent value beside HighLowBarCount: prevCycleMaxCount, latched when the count resets
count == 1 && justAdvanced && prevCycleMaxCount >= minPriorCount

complexity.reason: one additional latched integer on top of the HighLowBarCount state

rules.merge_notes: Single source, mined as research grade because it appeared to need 'a memory of prior setup TYPES, a new kind of state'. Under R17-01's counter it does not: the sequence H1(,H1), H2, then H1 again IS the counter reaching >= 2, resetting on a fresh N-bar high, and re-advancing to 1, so one latched integer covers it. That is why it is B and not C. Used NEGATED it is the filter Brooks states ('it is wise to wait'), so the per-placement toggle gives both readings. The 'final flag' framing R11-24 references is a three_push_patterns concept and is not carried.

rules.description: The second leg of the correction has run beyond the first leg's extreme: the running low since the count reached 2 is below the low retained when the count reached 1 (mirror: the running high above the count-1 high). Brooks: 'bears who shorted the first up leg will add as soon as the second leg up goes above the high of the first leg up.'
rules.pseudocode: count >= 2 && minLowSince < signalLowAtCountOne   // both values already retained by HighLowBarCount

complexity.reason: one extra retained price on top of the HighLowBarCount state; the comparison itself is trivial

rules.merge_notes: Single source. Mined as hard because it was framed in terms of leg 1 and leg 2 identified by pivots; under R17-01's counter the two legs' extremes are the values the counter already keeps (signalLow at each advance, and the running minimum since), so no pivots are needed. This is the EXPANDING correction - distinct from LegCountAtLeast, which only asks how many legs there have been, and from HighLowBarCount, whose advance guard asks for a new low since the last COUNTED bar rather than beyond the FIRST leg's extreme. Those two coincide for a strictly deepening pullback and diverge for a shallow second leg, which is exactly the case Brooks is separating.

rules.description: Block with-trend entries for blockBars bars after consecutive buy climaxes: no run of climaxCount consecutive climactic bull moves has completed within the last blockBars bars. Brooks: 'after three consecutive sell climaxes the market usually corrects sideways to up for at least 10 bars and with at least two legs.'
rules.pseudocode: barsSince(ConsecutiveClimaxBars fired) > blockBars

complexity.reason: a bars-since counter keyed on an existing climax detector

rules.merge_notes: Four statements of one block, unanimous on 10 bars and on 'at least two legs' as the expected correction. All four were mined at hard or research grade because 'climax' had no definition; bar_anatomy_trend_doji has since merged ConsecutiveClimaxBars as an authorable rule, so the only thing left here is the bars-since counter - hence B, not C. climaxCount 3 from RP1-14 and R22-15 (T21-40 and T21-71 say 'consecutive climaxes' and 'a buy climax' without a count, so 3 is the stated value and 1 is the loose reading). T21-71 adds the useful specific: after a climax a high 1 and maybe a high 2 will fail, so the block should lift at count >= 2 - that is HighLowBarCount ANDed, not a second rule. R22-15's session scoping ('the third consecutive sell climax of the day') is a time_session concern and is dropped; the bar window does the same work without a session reset. Carried as a filter, so a placement that wants the opposite reading (fade after three climaxes) uses the negate toggle.

rules.description: Block COUNTERTREND entries for blockBars bars after a spike: no run of spikeBars consecutive bull trend bars has completed within the last blockBars bars (mirror: no bear spike, blocking longs). Brooks: most traders who fade a spike lose, 'because most of the pullbacks do not fall far enough for a profit'.
rules.pseudocode: barsSince(spikeBars consecutive bull trend bars completed) > blockBars

complexity.reason: a bars-since counter keyed on the consecutive-trend-bar detector

rules.merge_notes: Single source. Same shape as PostClimaxCorrectionBlock but a different trigger event (a plain spike, bar_anatomy_trend_doji's ConsecutiveTrendBars, not a climax) and it blocks the OPPOSITE side, so it is not that rule with a parameter changed - the event detector lives inside the rule and the pane cannot substitute one for the other. Kept separate for that reason. TP3-41's page-310 note, 'after a strong breakout the bears might not look to sell again for dozens of bars', is the same test at a much larger blockBars and is why the input should be optimized rather than pinned at 10.

rules.description: Block new longs for blockBars bars after a failed new high: price closed above the highest high of the last N bars and then, within failBars bars, a bear trend bar closed back below that level. Brooks: assume the market trades down for at least a couple of legs and at least 10 bars.

complexity.reason: a retained breakout level, a bounded failure window and a countdown; the swing-high reference is replaced by the N-bar-extreme window

rules.merge_notes: Single source. Mined as hard on a swing-high reference; the fresh-N-bar-extreme window used elsewhere in this bucket replaces the pivot and drops it to moderate. The 10-bar, two-legged correction horizon is the same number PostClimaxCorrectionBlock carries, from a different trigger - kept separate because the trigger is a failed breakout, not a climax, and breakouts_pullback_retest owns the failure detector (FailedBreakoutReversal) that this could eventually be keyed on. TP3-23's other two outcomes on page 311 (enough follow-through = stay long; sideways = buy lower) are not conditions and are dropped.

rules.description: Brooks's BROAD pullback definition: any pause in the trend's momentum - the bar is an inside bar, OR a trend bar against the trend's direction, OR a doji. 'Any pause should be considered a pullback, even though there may be only sideways action and not an actual move backward.'
rules.pseudocode: isInsideBar(0) || close[0] < open[0] || abs(close[0] - open[0]) <= dojiBodyFraction * (high[0] - low[0])

complexity.reason: an OR of three single/two-bar OHLC tests

catalog_match.note: InsideBar is one of the three disjuncts; the catalog rule alone fires on strictly fewer bars

rules.merge_notes: Single source, and it must be one rule rather than three: the pane system ANDs entries, so an OR of three independently meaningful conditions is the one shape the pane CANNOT build from parts. Kept explicitly apart from PullbackBar (the strict lower-low definition) - Brooks states them as competing definitions in the same paragraph and says the broad one 'is more useful', but they fire on very different bar sets and nobody has measured the overlap. dojiBodyFraction is not in the source; bar_anatomy_trend_doji's DojiBar owns the threshold and this rule should take whatever that rule settles on.

rules.description: Allow high 1/2/3/4 buy setups only when the market is not in a clear bear trend (mirror: low 1/2/3/4 shorts only when not in a clear bull trend). Both remain valid inside a trading range. Brooks states this as the standing precondition on the whole counting family.
rules.pseudocode: !clearBearTrend()   // long side; the always-in read, whichever proxy the corpus adopts

complexity.reason: 'a clear bull/bear trend' is the always-in classification, an open design decision

rules.merge_notes: Two statements of the same gate, one from Ranges ch17 (where the counting family is defined) and one from ch26. R26-03 adds the trading-range half explicitly - a high 2 is valid in a bull trend OR at the bottom of a trading range, never in a bear trend - which is why the recommended reading is the NEGATIVE one (block only in the clearly opposite trend) rather than requiring a with-trend classification: the negative form needs only the always-in direction and not a separate trading-range detector. Blocked on the always-in decision, which three other buckets have already recommended settling as 'two consecutive strong trend bars flip the state'; this bucket concurs and needs nothing more than a direction.

rules.description: Trade the OPPOSITE side of a counting setup that forms against the trend: when a low 1-4 short setup forms inside a bull trend, buy at the level the mismatched short would have used as its trigger, since the odds are it fails and runs the protective buy stops above.
rules.pseudocode: clearBullTrend() && lowCount in 1..4 && justAdvanced && low[0] <= mismatchedTriggerLevel   // level = the low-N signal bar's low

complexity.reason: the counter is settled, but the channel/trend classification that makes the setup 'mismatched' is the always-in design decision

rules.merge_notes: Single source. The action half of CountSetupTrendGate: same mismatch condition, but rather than skipping the setup it takes the other side at the same price. Kept as a rule and not dropped as a composite because the ENTRY LEVEL is the mismatched setup's own trigger, which no ANDed pair of rules can express. Brooks's limit-order framing is mechanized as the level being touched; the corpus has no limit model, per the standing convention. Blocked on the same always-in decision as CountSetupTrendGate and on nothing else.

rules.description: Exit the with-trend swing once the trend itself has completed legsToComplete legs (default two) and price has reached the measured-move area. Brooks: 'two legs often complete a move, and the move is usually followed by at least a protracted countertrend move that has at least two legs.'
rules.pseudocode: withTrendLegCount >= legsToComplete && high[0] >= measuredMoveTarget - toleranceTicks * tickSize

complexity.reason: counts WITH-TREND legs, which R17-01's counter does not provide - that counter counts pullback legs and resets on every fresh trend extreme

catalog_match.note: same 'exit at a projected target' shape; the target here is a measured move off prior structure rather than K x ATR

rules.merge_notes: Single source, and the one rule in this bucket that the settled leg definition does NOT unblock. R17-01's counter is a PULLBACK counter: it resets to zero on every fresh N-bar extreme, so by construction it can never report how many legs the TREND has made. Counting with-trend legs needs either retained swing pivots (swing_structure's ring of four) or a second counter with the roles reversed, and no source in this bucket states one - hence C with its own design decision rather than B. The measured-move target half belongs to exits_targets and should be supplied from there rather than reinvented here.
design_decisions_needed: with-trend leg counting (distinct from pullback leg counting)

rules.description: The countertrend pullback into the setup is steep - its depth per bar exceeds a threshold - in which case Brooks says to skip the first reversal signal and wait for a second entry.
rules.pseudocode: (highest(high, lookback)[0] - low[0]) / barsSinceHigh >= steepSlopeThreshold

complexity.reason: 'steep' has no bar-level test in the source and no threshold; the units (points per bar, ATR per bar, fraction of the leg per bar) are not fixed either

rules.merge_notes: Single source. Everything in R19-03 except the word 'steep' is already carried: 'wait for the second entry' is SecondSignal and the higher-low signal bar is swing_structure's HigherLowBar, both ANDed by the pane. What is left is one undefined measure, so the rule is C and names it. swing_structure settled the DEPTH measure (PullbackDepthFromRecentHigh, drawdown from the running high over a fixed lookback); steepness is that depth divided by the bars it took, so the cheap resolution is to reuse that rule's window and add a per-bar denominator rather than invent a slope primitive. ATR per bar is the portable alternative and is why WFSafe_AvgTrueRange is listed.

rules.description: The one-bar pullback, Brooks's strict definition: in an uptrend the bar's low is below the prior bar's low by at least pullbackTicks (mirror: in a downtrend the high is above the prior bar's high). The building block the whole counting family is phrased in.
rules.pseudocode: low[0] <= low[1] - pullbackTicks * tickSize

complexity.reason: one two-bar comparison

catalog_match.note: at pullbackTicks = 1 (strictly below) this is exactly LaggedHigherHigh(lookback = 0)'s SHORT condition, low[0] < low[1], reached by the per-placement flip toggle - the same call swing_structure made for R11-08

rules.merge_notes: Six restatements of the same sentence across all three books; five are verbatim glossary copies. Do not author: the catalog rule covers it. The one thing the catalog rule does NOT cover is the TICK OFFSET - R00-14 (minTicks), RP3-01 (pullbackTicks) and R11-10 (limitOffsetTicks) all expose one, and at any value above 1 tick this stops being LaggedHigherHigh. All three default it to 1 and Brooks never uses another value, so the offset is recorded here rather than authored; if a deeper-dip form is ever wanted it is a new rule, not a change to LaggedHigherHigh. R11-10 is the same comparison in limit-order clothing ('buy on a limit below the low of the prior bar') - the corpus has no limit-fill model, and the standing convention mechanizes it as this bar test, so it adds no behaviour. Kept apart from PauseBarBroad and LowerHighPullbackBar, which are the book's two competing pullback definitions and fire on different bars.

rules.description: The one-legged pullback stated on the HIGHS: in a bull trend the bar's high is below the prior bar's high (mirror: the low above the prior bar's low). Brooks's other one-bar reading of a high 1 buy setup.
rules.pseudocode: high[0] < high[1]

complexity.reason: one two-bar comparison

catalog_match.note: LaggedHigherHigh(lookback = 0) NEGATED gives high[0] <= high[1] / low[0] >= low[1]; this rule is the strict form, so the two differ only on bars whose high exactly equals the prior high. Not worth a rule for the tie

rules.merge_notes: Single source. swing_structure already merged R11-06 ('the high of the current bar is at or below the high of the prior bar') into the catalog's LaggedHigherHigh at priority D; R11-09 is the same test with a strict inequality and gets the same treatment for consistency. Do not confuse with swing_structure's HigherLowBar, which is the SIDE-SWAPPED test (long on the lows, short on the highs) and genuinely is not reachable by the toggles - that one is authored, this one is not.

rules.description: At least one of the last N bars closed above its own open (mirror: below). Brooks's gate on a FIRST entry: 'bar 3 was a first entry long on a new low of the day, but after six bars without a bullish close it makes more sense to wait for a second long entry.'
rules.pseudocode: count over i in 1..lookback of (close[i] > open[i]) >= 1

complexity.reason: a counted comparison over a fixed window

catalog_match.note: ConsecutiveUpBars FLIPPED gives long = all N bars closed below their opens; NEGATED that is 'at least one closed above', exactly this rule. Both toggles are per-placement, so it is redundant by construction

rules.merge_notes: Single source, and its own miner spotted the equivalence ('equivalent to NOT ConsecutiveUpBars(6) on the short side'). Do not author. design_decisions.topic: leg definition - what advances a leg count (THIS BUCKET OWNS IT; other buckets defer here)
options: R17-01's persistent counter (Ranges ch17): a bar whose high exceeds the prior bar's high advances the count, but only once a new low has formed since the last counted bar; the count resets to 0 when the close makes a fresh N-bar high. No pivots, no lookahead, one Highest window and two retained prices.

Swing-pivot leg segmentation: detect SwingHigh/SwingLow at a given strength, then count alternating directional swings since the last trend extreme (R05-17, V24-03, TP1-05, T18-02, T20-02, V01-03). Needs pivot detection plus pivot retention, and every source that chose it was graded hard.

R00-60 / T00-19's counter: count each higher-high bar during a pullback, resetting 'when the pullback ends or the trend context changes' - the same machine as option 1 but with the reset left undefined, which is what made it research grade.
T20-01's explicit non-answer: Brooks says a leg ends on 'any criterion that you choose' - a minimum retracement, a trend-line break, or a pivot - and fixes none.
Per-chapter ad hoc counters that reset on a new trend high with a stated window: T10-23 (20 bars), T15-19 (10 bars), T21-72 (20 bars).
design_decisions.recommended: OPTION 1, R17-01, for the whole H1/H2/H3/H4 and L1/L2/L3/L4 family and for everything built on it. It is the most mechanizable version, exactly as MERGE.md anticipated: no swing pivots, no lookahead, no leg definition at all - the 'new low since the last counted bar' guard does the work a pivot search would do, and the fresh-N-bar-high reset does the work 'the trend's prior extreme' was left doing. Option 5 is independent corroboration rather than a rival: T10-23 arrives at the same machine with the same 20-bar reset from a different book. Option 2 is kept only as a citation - it costs pivot detection and pivot retention for no behaviour the counter does not already give, and it makes every rule downstream hard rather than moderate. Option 4 is why this had to be decided rather than mined. CONSEQUENCES, so other buckets can consume the decision without re-reading this file: (a) resetLookback defaults to 20 and is the family's one shared window; (b) the counter saturates at 4, Brooks's own cap; (c) the counter retains signalLow (the low of each counted bar) and minLowSince (the running low since), and FailedCountReversal, FailedCountSetupExit, SecondLegExceedsFirstLegExtreme and CountRestartAfterHighTwo are all free once those two values exist - which is why eleven rules in this bucket are B rather than C; (d) ABC corrections are this counter under another name and need no rule; (e) the counter counts PULLBACK legs only. It resets on every fresh trend extreme and therefore cannot report how many legs the TREND has made - that is a separate, still-open decision (below), and it is the only leg-count rule here the decision does not unblock. swing_structure independently reached the same conclusion and merged R17-01 under the same key, HighLowBarCount; the roll-up must fold the two entries into one rule.

design_decisions.topic: with-trend leg counting (how many legs the TREND has made, as opposed to the pullback)
options: Retained swing pivots - swing_structure's ring of four same-side pivots - counting alternating impulse swings since the trend began.
A second R17-01-style counter with the roles reversed (advance on a new extreme after an intervening pullback), running alongside the pullback counter.
Do not count trend legs at all: replace 'two legs are complete' with a measured-move or ATR target and drop the leg term.
design_decisions.recommended: Option 3 unless a source demands otherwise. R08-16 is the only candidate in this bucket that needs trend-leg counting, and what it actually trades is the measured-move target; the 'two legs' clause is Brooks's explanation of why the target tends to hold, not a second condition. Option 2 is the cheap fallback if a real rule ever needs the count, since it reuses machinery that will already exist. Option 1 costs pivot retention for one rule.

design_decisions.topic: what makes a signal 'the second entry' (setup identity and failure)
options: A generic per-placement registry: remember that THIS Entry candidate fired and failed within the last N bars (R00-52, V00-65, T00-21, T06-31, R26-06 - all research grade, all need engine support the corpus does not have).
T21-28's price proxy: the signal is a close above the prior bar's high, the failure is price trading back below that signal bar's low, and the scan is a bounded backward walk over the last N bars.
bar_anatomy_reversal_signal's narrower reading: track only the engine's own last Entry signal per placement.
design_decisions.recommended: OPTION 2, T21-28. It is the only one of the three that is authorable today, it needs no registry and no engine change, and it reproduces the second entries Brooks points at in the figures. Record the loss honestly: it counts a second GENERIC trigger, not a second instance of whichever pattern is placed beside it, so a placement that ANDs SecondSignal with a specific pattern gets 'that pattern, and some earlier trigger failed nearby' rather than 'that pattern twice'. If per-placement signal memory is ever added, option 1 supersedes it and option 3 is the intermediate step.

design_decisions.topic: always-in direction (needed only to gate the counting family by trend, not by this bucket's own primitives)
options: Two consecutive strong trend bars flip the state (the recommendation already made by bar_anatomy_trend_doji, breakouts_pullback_retest and bar_anatomy_reversal_signal).
Majority of the last N closes on one side of the EMA.
design_decisions.recommended: Concur with the three buckets that have already recommended it: two consecutive strong trend bars. Both rules blocked on it here need only a DIRECTION, never a strength score or a trading-range classification - R26-03's 'or at the bottom of a trading range' half is handled by stating the gate negatively (block only in the clearly OPPOSITE trend), which needs no range detector.

options: Depth per bar: swing_structure's PullbackDepthFromRecentHigh divided by the bars since the running high.
ATR per bar: the same drawdown expressed in WFSafe_AvgTrueRange units per bar, portable across instruments.
Fraction of the leg range per bar.
design_decisions.recommended: Option 2, ATR per bar, on the same portability grounds swing_structure used for its level tolerances - the corpus runs across symbols and a points-per-bar threshold does not survive that. R19-03 states no number at all, so whichever is chosen, the threshold is an optimizer input rather than a book value.

bucket_summary: 103 candidates, overwhelmingly restatements of one primitive: 23 of them (plus 5 strays sent from other buckets) are the H1/H2/L1/L2 bar counter, and they collapse into a single rule, HighLowBarCount, on R17-01's definition - the persistent counter that needs no swing pivots, no lookahead and no leg definition. Settling that as the canonical leg definition is what turns this bucket from a pile of research-grade candidates into eleven B rules: the counter already retains the signal-bar low and the running low since, so the failed-count reversal, the failed-count exit, the opposing-count exit, the expanding second leg and the count-restart trap all fall out of state that exists anyway. 23 rules out: 1 A (PauseBarBroad, the OR of inside/opposite/doji that the AND-ing pane cannot build from parts), 15 B, 4 C and 3 D. Three D rules are catalog duplicates - PullbackBar and LowerHighPullbackBar are LaggedHigherHigh(0) under the flip and negate toggles, RecentOppositeCloseExists is ConsecutiveUpBars under both - so the single most-quoted Brooks primitive is already in the corpus and needs no authoring. The four C rules are blocked on only three things, none of them the leg definition: always-in classification (two rules), with-trend leg counting as distinct from pullback leg counting (one), and an undefined 'steep' (one). 17 candidates dropped as compositions - almost all of them HighLowBarCount ANDed with an EMA touch, a range-extreme location or an always-in read, which the pane already does - and 17 sent to other buckets, mostly wedge, channel and trend-line material the keyword pass caught on the words 'second entry' and 'two legs'. ROLL-UP NOTE: swing_structure merged R17-01 under the same key HighLowBarCount and V21-04 under the same key OpposingCountExit; both pairs are one rule and must be folded, not authored twice.
